knowledge:
- key_parameters: plot=TRUE (in outlyx to plot multivariate outliers) ;; method='all' or method='horvath' (in agep to specify the epigenetic age predictor) ;; do_plot=TRUE (in estimateSex to plot predicted sex results) ;; referencePlatform="IlluminaHumanMethylation450k" or "IlluminaHumanMethylationEPIC" (in estimateCellCounts.wateRmelon to specify the array platform) ;; sex=pData(melon.pf)$sex (in seabi to specify sample sex) ;; X=fData(melon.pf)$CHR=='X' (in seabi to specify X-chromosome probes)
- alternatives: minfi package (and its read_metharray functions) can be used to read data into an RGChannelSet or MethylSet object instead of using readEPIC ;; adjustedFunnorm (only available for RGChannelSet) can be used instead of dasen ;; SWAN is another popular alternative normalization method mentioned
- when_to_use: Use this package when preprocessing raw Illumina 450k or EPIC DNA methylation microarray data, performing quality control, filtering poorly performing probes/samples, normalizing beta values, and predicting biological phenotypes (age, sex, cell-type proportions) for downstream EWAS.
- pitfalls: Epigenetic age predictions (agep) may show slight differences compared to original methods due to differences in normalization ;; genki (SNP genotype metric) is not available for minfi objects ;; adjusted_funnorm is only available for RGChannelSet objects ;; bisulfite conversion values (bscon) should ideally be above 90%, but above 80% is acceptable

workflows.name: dna_methylation_preprocessing_and_prediction
workflows.intent: Import, filter, normalize, and predict phenotypes from Illumina DNA methylation microarray data.
input: pheno_data (phenotype information corresponding to the IDAT files)
workflows.stages: 1. Import raw data using readEPIC ;; 2. Detect multivariate outliers using outlyx ;; 3. Check bisulfite conversion efficiency using bscon ;; 4. Filter poorly performing probes and samples using pfilter ;; 5. Predict epigenetic age using agep ;; 6. Predict sample sex using estimateSex ;; 7. Estimate blood cell-type proportions using estimateCellCounts.wateRmelon ;; 8. Normalize data using dasen ;; 9. Estimate normalization violence using qual ;; 10. Calculate performance metrics using dmrse_row, genki, and seabi ;; 11. Perform final probe-wise outlier detection sweep using pwod
workflows.code:
mlumi <- readEPIC('path/to/idats')
outliers <- outlyx(melon, plot=TRUE)
print(outliers)
# remove outliers with melon[,!outliers$out]
bsc <- bscon(melon)
hist(bsc, xlab = c(0, 100))
melon.pf <- pfilter(melon)
agep(melon, method='all')
agep(melon, method='horvath')
estimateSex(betas(melon), do_plot=TRUE)
estimateCellCounts.wateRmelon(melon, referencePlatform = "IlluminaHumanMethylation450k")
estimateCellCounts.wateRmelon(melon, referencePlatform = "IlluminaHumanMethylationEPIC") # change reference
dasen.melon <- dasen(melon) # Use whichever method you would like to use. 
das <- dasen(melon)
qu <- qual(betas(melon), betas(das))
plot(qu[,1], qu[,2])
dmrse_row(melon.pf)
dmrse_row(melon.dasen.pf) # Slightly better standard errores
genki(melon.pf)
genki(melon.dasen.pf)
seabi(melon.pf, sex=pData(melon.pf)$sex, X=fData(melon.pf)$CHR=='X')
seabi(melon.dasen.pf, sex=pData(melon.dasen.pf)$sex, X=fData(melon.dasen.pf)$CHR=='X')
bet <- betas(melon)
pwod_bet <- pwod(bet)
